hero.description: HeritageGraph is a platform by CAIR-Nepal for documenting cultural heritage — with a focus on Nepalese and Himalayan heritage — and publishing it as Linked Open Data modelled in CIDOC-CRM.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.paragraph1: Cultural heritage is the living memory of communities — traditions, artifacts, stories, and practices that connect the present to the past. Much of it remains undocumented, fragmented across institutions, or at risk of being lost.
mission.paragraph2: builds an interconnected digital record of that heritage using knowledge graph technologies. Publishing heritage data as Linked Open Data following CIDOC-CRM lets researchers, communities, and institutions trace connections, cite sources, and reuse the material under clear terms.

knowledgeGraph.desc: Interactive graph view over the CIDOC-CRM model, showing how records connect.

linkedOpenData.title: Linked Open Data
linkedOpenData.desc: Persistent w3id.org identifiers, RDF content negotiation, and a public SPARQL endpoint.

communityCuration.title: Community curation
communityCuration.desc: Contributions from community members, scholars, and institutions, each attributed and versioned.

epistemicReview.title: Epistemic review
epistemicReview.desc: Claims carry sources and confidence, and are reviewed before publication. How that works is documented on the methods page.

data.title: How the data is governed
data.description: What a reader, reviewer, or reuser needs to know before relying on these records.

provenance.definition: Imported sources are kept in frozen, separately named graphs. Curated claims carry a data source and a confidence value, so every published statement can be traced to where it came from.

access.definition: Records can be marked public, restricted, community-only, or culturally sensitive. The SPARQL proxy filters restricted material rather than relying on the interface to hide it.

licensing.definition: Software is MIT-licensed. Data carries per-source terms — OpenStreetMap, Wikidata, UNESCO and community contributions differ, and the applicable licence travels with each source.

identifiers.definition: Entities receive persistent w3id.org IRIs. External alignments are recorded as explicit links rather than silent merges.

standards.title: Built on published standards
standards.description: The model is not bespoke: it reuses established heritage and semantic web vocabularies so the data is interoperable with other archives.

review.heading: Review model
review.intro: Contributions are reviewed by people holding one of three reviewer personas, recorded on ReviewerRole with an expertise area and an active flag. Capability is cumulative: each persona can do everything the one above it can.

communityReviewer.name: Community reviewer
communityReviewer.can: Approve clear-cut contributions, request changes, escalate to an expert.
communityReviewer.cannot: Adjust confidence scores, or resolve conflicting claims.

domainExpert.name: Domain expert
domainExpert.can: Verify claims, adjust confidence, reconcile conflicting evidence.
domainExpert.cannot: Supersede records, merge locked identities, or assign reviewer roles.

expertCurator.name: Expert curator
expertCurator.can: Reconcile identity, supersede records, export data, manage verifications, assign reviewer roles.
expertCurator.cannot: Approve a merge request they opened themselves.

review.assignment: <term>Assignment</term> — roles are granted by another user and recorded with the granting account, so reviewer authority is itself auditable.
review.separationOfDuties: Separation of duties — CannotApproveOwnMergeRequest blocks the account that opened a merge request from approving it, at the object-permission level rather than in the interface.
review.publicationGate: Publication gate — only accepted, merged and published rows reach the public graph. Unknown status values are withheld by default rather than allowed.
review.labelGate: <term>Label gate</term> — a row without a real name is withheld even if approved, so a stray keystroke cannot become a node in the graph or a pin on the atlas.
review.identityLock: <term>Identity locks</term> — merging into a locked cluster, or over a recorded conflict, requires an expert curator.
review.selectivityCaveat: Reviewer selectivity has not yet been characterised: the acceptance rate over the current corpus is not a meaningful measure at this sample size, and no inter-reviewer agreement has been computed. Do not cite an acceptance rate from this deployment as evidence of review rigour.

fair.heading: FAIR + CARE
fair.findable: Findable — w3id resource IRIs; VoID/DCAT dataset description; corpus fingerprint (manage.py corpus_fingerprint).
fair.accessible: Accessible — HTTPS dereference plus a CARE-aware read-only SPARQL endpoint (/sparql/).
fair.interoperable: <term>Interoperable</term> — CIDOC-CRM, CRMinf, LinkML registry, CRM bridge, SHACL shapes, SKOS vocabularies.
fair.reusable: <term>Reusable</term> — license matrix below; frozen L0 dump with SHA-256; idempotent L1 ETL; ontology pin in import reports.
fair.care: CARE — access_tier and TK labels on sources; sensitive tiers are filtered by the SPARQL proxy, not merely hidden in the interface. Community consent governance is not yet in place — see limitations.
fair.checklist: Full machine-readable checklist: documentation/research/NATURE_KG_RIGOR.md; ethics and consent status: documentation/research/ETHICS_AND_CONSENT.md.

model.heading: Ontology & graph model
model.schema: Schema: LinkML registry generated from ontology/HeritageGraph.yaml (CIDOC-CRM bridge, SHACL shapes, SKOS vocabularies).
model.namedGraph: Published instances live in the named graph {graph}.
model.museumView: Museum live view: SPARQL projection via GET /api/v1/cidoc/kg/graph/?scope=reviewed — nodes typed by rdf:type, edges are asserted triples rather than client-side heuristics.
model.lux: External Yale LUX bulk import stays in imported/lux; only entities linked with skos:exactMatch appear in the museum. It is a linkset, not a merge into the public partition.
model.twoLayer: Large research dumps (DANAM-aligned N-Quads) use a two-layer policy: frozen L0 named graphs for citation and SPARQL, plus curated L1 materialisation into graph/public. See documentation/research/DANAM_CORPUS_INTEGRATION_REPORT.md.

corpusPin.heading: DANAM corpus pin
corpusPin.l0Value: manage.py rdf_load_imported_nq (never writes to the public graph)

pipeline.heading: Publication pipeline
pipeline.save: Contributions are saved in Django — cultural entities, CIDOC metadata, and relationship assertions.
pipeline.review: Review by a qualified persona, as described above; only terminal approval states pass the publication gate.
pipeline.project: kg_publish / rdf_rebuild project triples into Oxigraph; the provenance partition records agent and source.
pipeline.integrity: Integrity gate: kg_rigor_audit checks namespace, connectivity, pollution, L0 isolation, and provenance coverage. Use --strict for a release.
pipeline.evaluate: Evaluation: kg_evaluate against an expert gold standard. Runs mark themselves reportable: false when the gold set is too small or absent, and those figures must not be cited.

limitations.heading: Limitations
limitations.corpusSize: The corpus is community-curated and growing — it is not a complete national inventory.
limitations.temporal: Temporal coverage (EDTF) is incomplete on many event nodes.
limitations.reconciliation: External identifier reconciliation (Wikidata, Getty) is in progress beyond DANAM sameAs.
limitations.demoCorpus: The museum demo corpus is illustrative only; cite the live reviewed graph for research.
limitations.doi: No Zenodo DOI has been minted yet. Cite the repository and the corpus SHA-256 above in the interim.
limitations.shacl: SHACL-on-write is opt-in (RDF_SHACL_VALIDATE_ON_WRITE); shapes are generated and available for offline conformance reports.
limitations.evaluation: No reportable precision/recall evaluation exists yet: the gold standard has not been annotated. Any evaluation figures currently produced are marked not reportable.
limitations.consent: A formal community consent process and institutional ethics review have not been completed. Culturally sensitive classes are withheld from public query results pending that work.

lux.body: Yale University Art Gallery LUX data is used under its terms as a linked external authority. HeritageGraph stores stubs in imported/lux and links curated entities with skos:exactMatch; Yale IRIs are not served as an isolated dump in the museum view.

scoring.heading: How scoring works
scoring.formulaLead: Each contribution earns a base score for its type. Contributions older than the grace period decay exponentially, so a score reflects sustained participation rather than a one-off burst.

t.meaning: Days since the contribution was created.

lambda.meaning: Decay constant. Decay applies only beyond the grace period.

grace.meaning: Grace period. Contributions newer than this keep their full base score.

scoring.medalBand: {medal} — awarded to contributors in the top {percentile}% of the register by current score.
scoring.caveat: Medals and tiers are derived from position and point totals only. They record participation, not the accuracy or scholarly value of any contribution — that is what the review process is for. Do not cite a tier or medal as a quality signal.

register.footnote: The register lists the top 50 contributors and is recomputed at most every 5 minutes. Ranking reflects volume and recency of participation, not contribution quality.

scoring.title: How this ranking is scored
scoring.lead: Lifetime contribution volume — every contribution counts at full weight, regardless of age. This is a different measure from the current score on
scoring.leadSuffix: , which applies time decay. The two ranks will differ.

knowledgeList.statusNote: Every row shows its review status. Only accepted and merged records are published to the public graph; pending and rejected rows are visible here for transparency but are not part of the citable dataset.

entity.title: Cultural entities
entity.definition: Any documented item of cultural heritage — an object, place, practice or record — modelled as a CIDOC-CRM entity. This is the broadest class in the registry; the more specific classes below are subsets of it.

person.title: Historical persons
person.definition: Individuals recorded in the heritage record: rulers, artisans, donors, priests and chroniclers. Modelled on CIDOC-CRM E21 Person.

location.title: Heritage locations
location.definition: Places with a recorded heritage significance, carrying coordinates where these are known. Coordinate provenance is stated per record.

event.title: Cultural events
event.definition: Datable occurrences — construction, consecration, destruction, restoration — that connect entities to periods and places.

period.title: Historical periods
period.definition: Named spans of time used to date entities and events, such as dynastic or architectural periods.

tradition.title: Traditions and practices
tradition.definition: Living or recorded intangible heritage: rituals, crafts, performance and oral practice.

source.title: Documentary sources
source.definition: Publications, archives, manuscripts, surveys and interviews cited as evidence for assertions in the graph.

deity.title: Deities
deity.definition: Divine figures venerated at documented sites, linked to the entities and events that invoke them.

guthi.title: Guthi
guthi.definition: Newar community trusts that hold responsibility for the upkeep and ritual life of heritage sites.

structure.title: Architectural structures
structure.definition: Built heritage — temples, courtyards, water systems and monuments — with their construction and condition history.

monument.title: Monuments
monument.definition: Structures designated or recorded as monuments, including their protection status where known.

ritual.title: Ritual events
ritual.definition: Recurring religious observances tied to particular places, deities and communities.

festival.title: Festivals
festival.definition: Calendar festivals documented with their locations, participants and associated practices.

iconography.title: Iconographic objects
iconography.definition: Images and sculptural programmes described by their iconographic content and attributions.

unescoEntry.listSummary: Nepal has four properties on the UNESCO World Heritage List — two cultural, two natural.
unescoEntry.serialNote: A serial property of seven monument zones.
unescoEntry.zonesCaution: These are the seven monument zones of one property — not seven World Heritage Sites.
unescoEntry.boundaryConfirmed: Zone boundaries confirmed by the World Heritage Committee in 2006.
unescoEntry.dangerListing: Placed on the List of World Heritage in Danger in 2003; removed in 2007.
unescoEntry.scopeHeading: What this page does not cover
unescoEntry.scopeBody: This page covers Nepal's two cultural properties. Sagarmatha National Park (1979) and Chitwan National Park (1984) are inscribed as natural properties, and fall outside a record scoped to cultural heritage.
unescoEntry.graphBoundaryBody: HeritageGraph records far more than the World Heritage List — Guthi institutions, ritual cycles, the Kumari lifecycle, syncretic relations. Nothing outside the list is UNESCO-inscribed, and this record never implies otherwise.
unescoEntry.noPhotographRecorded: No photograph recorded for this subject.
unescoEntry.provenanceNote: Photography from Wikimedia Commons, retrieved {date}. Each image carries its licence and author.
unescoEntry.factsSourceNote: Inscription facts on this page come from the UNESCO World Heritage List. Entity records come from the reviewed HeritageGraph knowledge graph.
